Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available
changes.detail: Amazon EMR 8.2 is now available with new features across Amazon EMR on EC2, Amazon EMR on EKS, and Amazon EMR Serverless. This release upgrades Apache Spark to 4.1.3, Apache Iceberg to 1.11.0, and Delta Lake to 4.2.0, and it is designated a Long Term Support (LTS) release. This release makes it easier to run secure, governed analytics at scale — you can now write to the same Delta Lake table on Amazon S3 from multiple clusters concurrently, refresh Iceberg materialized views incrementally, and propagate end-user identity from Spark jobs and interactive sessions all the way to AWS Lake Formatio

changes.title: Introducing the Apache Spark Optimization Agent for Amazon EMR Serverless
changes.detail: Amazon EMR Serverless now offers the Apache Spark optimization agent, which analyzes completed Spark job runs and delivers cost and performance optimization recommendations in seconds. You can select a cost or performance goal, and the agent returns specific configuration changes with the telemetry evidence and plain-language reasoning behind each suggestion. The agent can analyze a single run or compare it against a known-good baseline to pinpoint what changed. changes.title: Amazon DynamoDB caching is now available with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey
changes.detail: Today, AWS announces the general availability of DynamoDB caching with Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey, enabling sub-millisecond read latency for frequently accessed DynamoDB data. Previously, if you required faster reads than DynamoDB's single-digit millisecond latency, you had to manually manage cache infrastructure or keep a separate cache in sync. Now you can access DynamoDB table data from a write-through cache that updates as data changes and automatically scales to meet changing workload demands. DynamoDB caching requires no application logic changes and minimal configuration.
